description: CIS Critical Controls - Safeguards to defend against cyber attacks

CIS-1.title: Inventory and Control of Enterprise Assets
CIS-1.description: Actively manage all hardware devices and software assets connected to the network so that only authorized devices are given access and unauthorized and unmanaged devices are found and isolated.

subcontrols.title: Establish and Maintain Detailed Asset Inventory
subcontrols.description: Establish and maintain an accurate, detailed, and up-to-date inventory of all assets connected to the network

subcontrols.title: Address Unauthorized Assets
subcontrols.description: Ensure that a process exists to address unauthorized assets on the network

CIS-2.title: Software Asset Management
CIS-2.description: Actively manage all software on enterprise assets using a disciplined processes for discovery, evaluation and decommissioning of software.

CIS-3.title: Data Protection
CIS-3.description: Protect data by implementing and managing appropriate technical, procedural and physical controls.

CIS-4.title: Secure Configuration Management
CIS-4.description: Establish and maintain the security configuration of enterprise assets (hardware, software, infrastructure and software-as-a-service) based on industry-supported and documented hardening standards.

CIS-5.title: Access Control Management
CIS-5.description: Use processes and technology to manage identity, authentication and access (authorization) to cloud and on-premises infrastructure and applications.

CIS-6.title: Logging and Monitoring
CIS-6.description: Collect, manage and analyze audit logs for the activities of users, administrators, systems and other components of the IT environment.

CIS-7.title: Email and Web Browser Protections
CIS-7.description: Protect against phishing, malicious content, and other web-based threats by implementing technical and process controls on web browsers and email systems.

CIS-8.title: Malware Defenses
CIS-8.description: Prevent or control the installation, execution, propagation of malicious applications, code or scripts.

CIS-9.title: Service Provider Management
CIS-9.description: Ensure the confidentiality, integrity and availability of information and systems are protected at service providers.

CIS-10.title: Data Recovery Capabilities
CIS-10.description: Recover the enterprise's information systems to a known effective state after a security event.

CIS-11.title: Network Infrastructure Management
CIS-11.description: Establish, implement and actively manage network infrastructure to protect enterprise assets.

CIS-12.title: Boundary Defense
CIS-12.description: Detect and prevent unauthorized data exfiltration or misuse of enterprise assets connected to the internet.

CIS-13.title: Network Monitoring and Defense
CIS-13.description: Detect, investigate and respond to security events and incidents on the network.

CIS-14.title: Security Awareness and Skills Training
CIS-14.description: Establish and maintain a program to educate and train all personnel, including those without technical roles.

CIS-15.title: Service and Supportability
CIS-15.description: Identify, select and procure tools that support controlled assessment and monitoring of security controls.

CIS-16.title: Application Software Security
CIS-16.description: Manage the security of information systems applications and web services.

CIS-17.title: Incident Response Management
CIS-17.description: Establish a program to promptly identify, investigate, internally report on, and respond to security incidents.

CIS-18.title: Penetration Testing and Red Team Exercises
CIS-18.description: Test the effectiveness of security controls by conducting regular penetration testing.

CIS-19.title: Threat Intelligence Program
CIS-19.description: Establish a program for continuous threat intelligence gathering and sharing.

CIS-20.title: Security Orchestration and Response
CIS-20.description: Establish a capability to coordinate responses to security events.

IG1.name: Implementation Group 1
IG1.description: Often referred to as 'foundational', these controls are applicable to all organizations and represent the basic level of security controls that every organization should implement.

IG2.name: Implementation Group 2
IG2.description: Often referred to as 'intermediate', these controls apply to most organizations with moderate business value and should be implemented by enterprises.

IG3.name: Implementation Group 3
IG3.description: Often referred to as 'advanced', these controls should be implemented by organizations with high value data and critical infrastructure.
